scope_elements: Facility assessment of approximately 81 buildings within NSWDG compound to establish fire flow and fire water demand requirements
Documentation of two existing water systems: high-pressure non-potable fire main and Installation domestic water distribution system
Field investigation including hydrant flow tests, system valve assessments, pipe identification surveys
Development of hydraulic models (Bentley WaterGEMS) for both water distribution systems
Identification of deficiencies relative to UFC 3-600-01 requirements
Analysis and recommendations with ROM cost estimates for five NAVFAC-selected deficiencies
Non-potable water distribution system maintenance program

key_findings.high_pressure_system: High-pressure system (served by Fire Pump Station 352 and Water Storage Tank 351, 200,000 gal) generally adequate to support fire water demands for the 14 sprinklered buildings served; system delivers approximately 1,900 gpm at 20 psi residual. Two dead-end service mains are non-compliant with UFC 3-600-01.
key_findings.domestic_system: Domestic water system capable of approximately 1,650 gpm at 20 psi residual; inadequate for approximately 10 buildings with fire flow demands exceeding 1,650 gpm. Water Storage Tank 531 (250,000 gal elevated) lacks sufficient reserve for fire flow beyond daily domestic demand (only ~50,000 gal available for fire). Dead-end service main to Building 250 compound is non-compliant.

recommendations_with_rom_costs.item: Reprogram SCADA to increase domestic system operating pressures
recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Increase pump station set point pressures to raise fire flow from 1,650 gpm to ~1,900 gpm
recommendations_with_rom_costs.quote: ROM Cost: $0 construction costs. Only labor to reprogram the SCADA system.

recommendations_with_rom_costs.item: New 250,000-gallon elevated water storage tank at north end of NSWDG Compound
recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Supplement domestic system storage capacity; increase fire flow from 1,650 gpm to ~2,500 gpm

recommendations_with_rom_costs.item: Replace 450,000-gallon elevated water storage tank (replacing Tank 531)
recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Replace existing Tank 531 with larger tank; increase fire flow ~14%
recommendations_with_rom_costs.quote: ($3,351,723). Replace the elevated Water Storage Tank 531 with a new 450,000-gallon elevated storage tank.

recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Replace 1960s-era Pump Station 329, increase pumping from 240 gpm to 600 gpm, relocate to north end of compound

recommendations_with_rom_costs.item: Eliminate dead-end service main serving Building 250 compound
recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Install new 8-inch water main connecting Building 250 distribution loop to Installation water system via directional drill under Redwing Lake

recommendations_with_rom_costs.item: Install seven new fire hydrants and supporting piping
recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Correct most significant fire hydrant spacing deficiencies; approximately 44 buildings deficient in hydrant coverage

recommendations_with_rom_costs.item: Disconnect seven high-pressure hydrants and reconnect to domestic/potable system
recommendations_with_rom_costs.description: Consolidate hydrants under single potable system, eliminate cross-contamination risk

taxonomy.taxonomy_notes: This is a study/site engineering investigation task order under a NAVFAC IQ A-E contract for fire protection projects. BFA held the prime contract with NAVFAC; Jacobs Engineering served as subconsultant. The 'design_bid_build' delivery method applies to the underlying IQ vehicle, though this was a study-only task order with no construction. program_type set to military_defense / military_operations for the NSWDG special operations compound context.

drawings.notes: No standalone drawing set present in intake folder. The study report PDF (Study Fire Protection Systems at NSWDG Compound.pdf) contains embedded figures including site maps, water system diagrams (Appendices A–C), facility summary sheets (Appendix D), and hydraulic model node diagrams (Appendix K), but these are report figures embedded in the text PDF, not a separately rendered drawing set.
